description: Crypto Basis/Carry — Dated (Quarterly) Futures vs Spot. Structurally different mechanism from Direction D's perpetual funding-rate carry: this tests whether the futures-minus-spot basis on a FIXED-EXPIRY (quarterly) contract — which must converge to zero at expiry by construction — offers a collectible, cost-positive, statistically real annualized carry return via long-spot/short-future cash-and-carry. Distinct from Direction E's cointegration pairs (spread between two DIFFERENT assets) and Direction D's funding (a periodic payment stream on a perpetual, no fixed expiry/convergence date).
current_verdict_2026-07-29: REJECTED. Trial #6001's primary (returns-based, stationary) Newey-West test never distinguishes realized delta-neutral carry from zero (p>0.4 in all 8 symbol/venue/window combinations tested), and the deterministic snapshot-hold-to-expiry basis never clears the assumed T-bill yield net of realistic costs on BTC or ETH via either Binance-native or Deribit dated futures. Weaker result than Direction D's funding-arb (#4003, FAIL_RIGOR): here the mechanism itself is not statistically established, not merely insufficient after costs. Do not deploy real capital to this strategy.
stopping_rule_doc: Same standard as Direction D Trial #4003: net-of-realistic-cost annualized carry must (a) be statistically distinguishable from zero via Newey-West HAC test on the STATIONARY daily delta-neutral return series (spot_return - future_return), NOT on the basis level itself (a dated future's basis is a near-unit-root series that decays deterministically toward zero at expiry — an HAC test on the level series would show spurious significance and must not be used as the deciding test; it is reported only for transparency/comparison), and (b) beat the assumed T-bill yield after costs. Cross-exchange corroboration (Binance-native vs Binance-spot/Deribit-future) required, using the SAME expiry (2026-09-25) on both venues.
sacred_holdout_path: N/A — same rationale as Direction D: this is a measurement of a market-structure fact (realized historical basis/carry), not a fitted predictive model being confirmed on a holdout.

Deribit has no true spot market (derivatives-only exchange); Binance BTC/USDT and ETH/USDT spot is used as the cash leg for BOTH the Binance-native and the Deribit-future variants, so the only thing that varies across the two variants is the futures leg's venue.
No API keys, no order execution, no capital at risk. Public ccxt endpoints only (OHLCV history).

hypotheses.name: Crypto Quarterly Futures Basis/Carry — Rigor Pass (returns-NW significance, cost-stress, cross-exchange, T-bill)
hypotheses.status: REJECTED — realized carry not statistically distinguishable from zero on the valid (returns-based) test; snapshot hold-to-expiry basis never clears T-bill net of cost on any of the 4 symbol/venue combinations tested

result_summary.methodology: Primary test is Newey-West HAC on the stationary daily return r_t = spot_return_t - future_return_t (long-spot/short-future delta-neutral P&L). A secondary naive test on the raw annualized-basis LEVEL series is also reported to show the expected spurious-significance divergence -- it is NOT used to decide the verdict.

returns_based_nw_test_all_combos_NOT_sig.note: Every p-value is >0.4 (several >0.9) -- the realized daily carry P&L is statistically indistinguishable from noise in all 8 window/venue/symbol combinations. This is a materially WEAKER result than Direction D's funding-arb (Trial #4003), where the mean funding rate WAS Newey-West significant (p<0.05 everywhere) and the failure was purely a cost/T-bill-hurdle issue. Here, the existence of a real edge itself is not statistically established.

naive_level_based_nw_test_COMPARISON_ONL.note: As predicted before running: the level series (basis annualized per day) gives spuriously huge t-stats (9.2 to 19.96, p=0.0 in all 4 full-window combos) purely because the basis level is a near-unit-root series decaying toward 0 at expiry -- NOT because there is a real, tradeable edge. This divergence from the returns-based test (t-stats 0.05-0.68, all non-significant) is itself the key methodological finding: a level-based significance test on a dated future's basis would have produced a false-positive 'PASS' if it had been used as the decision test.

snapshot_hold_to_expiry_deterministic_nu.note: This is the cleanest, most decision-relevant number (a deterministic 'what would I earn if I opened this trade today and held to the 2026-09-25 expiry' projection, no significance test needed since it is not a sample mean). It NEVER clears the assumed 4.5%/yr T-bill yield net of realistic costs, on either symbol or either venue.

cross_exchange_consistency.detail: Binance-native (clean, same-venue, same-day-boundary) shows a thin, non-significant 2.3-3.2% raw full-window realized carry. Binance-spot-vs-Deribit-future shows a much larger 6-15% realized carry, but this is ALSO non-significant (p=0.92-0.96) and is the pre-registered-as-a-risk cross-venue tracking-noise scenario (inverse-contract quoting, ~8h daily-candle boundary offset between Binance 00:00 UTC and Deribit 08:00 UTC) rather than a real, corroborated basis. The two venues do NOT agree on a real, tradeable number; if anything the larger Deribit figure is evidence of measurement noise, not a bigger edge.
cross_exchange_consistency.crash_window_caveat: Dated futures do not persist back to 2020/2022; no real historical crash-window test was possible (contract history starts 2025-09-26 at the earliest). Trial #4003 (Direction D, funding-rate) remains the best available crypto-derivatives crash-window evidence. An informal 'largest in-window drawdown day' color check (BTC -6.5% to -14% single-day moves within the observed window) showed basis staying positive (0.7-5.9%) on those days -- informal color only, not equivalent to a real crash-window stress test.

result_summary.verdict: REJECTED. The primary, valid (returns-based, stationary) Newey-West test never rejects the null of zero mean carry across 8 symbol/venue/window combinations (all p>0.4). The deterministic snapshot-to-expiry basis, the cleanest available number, never beats the assumed T-bill yield net of realistic costs on any of the 4 symbol/venue combinations. Cross-exchange results do not corroborate each other. This is a WEAKER result than Direction D's funding-arb rigor pass (#4003, FAIL_RIGOR): here the underlying mechanism itself is not statistically distinguishable from noise over the available sample, not merely insufficient after costs.

hypotheses.instrument: BTC and ETH: Binance spot (BTC/USDT, ETH/USDT) as cash leg vs. (a) Binance quarterly dated future BTC/USDT:USDT-260925 / ETH/USDT:USDT-260925 [native, same venue] and (b) Deribit quarterly dated future BTC/USD:BTC-260925 / ETH/USD:ETH-260925 [cross-venue corroboration], both expiring 2026-09-25T08:00:00Z.
hypotheses.hypothesis: The futures-minus-spot basis on a fixed-expiry quarterly BTC/ETH future, captured via a delta-neutral long-spot/short-future cash-and-carry position, produces a realized annualized return that is (1) statistically distinguishable from zero on a stationary daily-P&L basis (Newey-West HAC on spot_return - future_return, not on the raw basis level), (2) durable across two independent venues for the same expiry, and (3) exceeds realistic round-trip trading costs and the assumed T-bill yield.
hypotheses.mechanism: Structural: a dated future must converge to spot at expiry (cash/physical settlement). If the future trades above spot (contango, the typical crypto regime), a long-spot/short-future position captures that convergence as the future's price decays toward spot over the contract's remaining life, independent of the direction spot itself moves (delta-neutral). This is DIFFERENT from Direction D's funding-rate mechanism (a periodic payment between long/short perpetual holders with no fixed expiry) even though both are 'carry' in the loose sense — basis/carry here is driven by time-to-expiry convergence, not a funding payment schedule.

hypotheses.crash_window_caveat: Dated futures contracts do not persist across years (they are listed ~6-12 months before their own expiry and then cease to exist), so this contract cannot reach back to the 2020 COVID crash or the 2022 LUNA/Celsius/FTX windows the way the perpetual funding-rate series in Trial #4003 could. This trial reports a 'largest in-window single-day drawdown' as informal color only, and defers to Trial #4003's funding-based crash results as the best available crypto-derivatives crash evidence.
